name: APOEL FC
content:
APOEL FC is one of the most successful and popular football clubs in Cyprus, based in the capital city of Nicosia. The club was founded in 1926 and has since become a dominant force in Cypriot football, winning numerous domestic league titles and cups. APOEL is especially known for its long-standing rivalry with Omonia Nicosia, a fixture that is considered the most important derby in Cypriot football due to its sporting intensity and historical, social, and political undertones.

On the European stage, APOEL has achieved several remarkable milestones that have raised the profile of Cypriot football. The club regularly competes in UEFA competitions such as the Champions League, Europa League, and Conference League. Its most historic achievement came in the 2011–12 UEFA Champions League season, when APOEL reached the quarter-finals, famously eliminating Olympique Lyonnais in the round of 16 on penalties and becoming one of the biggest underdog stories in modern European football.

Domestically, APOEL has consistently been one of the strongest teams in Cyprus, often competing for the league title and winning it multiple times across different eras. The club plays its home matches at the GSP Stadium in Nicosia, the largest stadium in Cyprus, which it shares with other local clubs. With a strong fan base, a history of success, and regular participation in European competitions, APOEL remains a central figure in Cypriot football identity.

name: AC Omonia
content:
AC Omonia is a Cypriot professional football club based in Nicosia, founded in 1948. The club was created by former APOEL players and other members who broke away for political and social reasons during a period of division in Cypriot sports. Omonia joined the Cyprus Football Association in 1953 and has since become one of the most popular and historically significant clubs in the country.

Domestically, Omonia is one of Cyprus’ most successful teams, winning numerous league titles, cups, and super cups. The club enjoyed its golden eras mainly in the 1970s and 1980s, when it dominated Cypriot football with multiple consecutive championships and cup victories. It is also known for its strong fan base and intense rivalry with APOEL, which is considered the biggest derby in Cypriot football.

On the European stage, Omonia has regularly participated in UEFA competitions, including the Champions League and Europa League, although with limited deep runs compared to domestic success. The club plays its home matches at the GSP Stadium in Nicosia, which it shares with APOEL and other local teams. Beyond football, Omonia operates several other sports departments, making it a multi-sport club with a significant presence in Cypriot athletics.

name: Anorthosis Famagusta FC
content:
Anorthosis Famagusta FC is one of the oldest and most historically significant football clubs in Cyprus. It was founded in 1911 in the city of Famagusta and is part of a broader multi-sport club. After the Turkish invasion of Cyprus in 1974, the club was forced to relocate and is now based in Larnaca, where it plays its home matches at the Antonis Papadopoulos Stadium. Despite this displacement, Anorthosis has maintained a strong identity and a large fan base across the island.

The club is considered one of the traditional “big teams” in Cypriot football and has won multiple domestic titles, including league championships, cups, and super cups. Anorthosis has a long-standing rivalry with other major Cypriot clubs, especially APOEL and AC Omonia, which are central to the country’s football culture. Over the decades, it has consistently competed at the top level of Cypriot football and has never been relegated from the top division.

On the European stage, Anorthosis is best known for its historic 2008–09 UEFA Champions League campaign, when it became the first Cypriot club to reach the group stage. During that run, the club eliminated strong opponents in qualifying and competed against major European teams, earning international recognition. This achievement remains one of the greatest milestones in Cypriot football history and significantly raised the club’s profile abroad.

name: AEL Limassol
content:
AEL Limassol is one of the oldest and most successful football clubs in Cyprus, based in the city of Limassol. The club was founded on 4 October 1930 and quickly became one of the founding members of Cypriot organized football competitions. Over time, AEL developed into a major force in Cypriot football, building a strong identity and a large supporter base. It is also part of a broader multi-sport club that includes departments such as basketball, volleyball, and futsal.

Domestically, AEL has enjoyed significant success, winning multiple Cypriot First Division titles, Cypriot Cups, and Super Cups. The club’s most successful periods came in different eras, establishing it as one of the traditional “big teams” in Cyprus. AEL is also known for its strong rivalry with other Limassol and Cypriot clubs, especially Apollon Limassol, which adds intensity to local derbies and contributes to the club’s strong football culture.

On the European stage, AEL has regularly participated in UEFA competitions such as the Champions League and Europa League. One of its most notable achievements was reaching the UEFA Europa League group stage in the 2012–13 season, marking an important milestone for the club at international level. The team plays its home matches at modern stadiums in Limassol and continues to be an important representative of Cypriot football in Europe.

name: AEK Larnaca FC
content:
AEK Larnaca FC is a Cypriot professional football club based in the city of Larnaca. It was founded in 1994 following the merger of two historic local clubs, EPA Larnaca and Pezoporikos Larnaca. This unification aimed to create a stronger football entity in the city, combining the traditions and achievements of both predecessor clubs. Since its formation, AEK has developed into one of the main forces in Cypriot football.

Domestically, AEK Larnaca has established itself as a consistent top-tier team in Cyprus, regularly competing for league positions, cup titles, and European qualification spots. While the club does not have as many championships as some traditional Cypriot giants, it has built a reputation for stability and competitiveness. Its home matches are played at the AEK Arena – Georgios Karapatakis Stadium, a modern venue that reflects the club’s recent growth and ambitions.

On the European stage, AEK has become increasingly visible in UEFA competitions. The club has participated in tournaments such as the UEFA Europa League, Champions League qualifiers, and UEFA Europa Conference League, achieving notable runs in recent years, including reaching the knockout stages of European competitions. This international experience has strengthened the club’s profile and confirmed its status as one of Cyprus’s most competitive modern teams.

name: Apollon Limassol FC
content:
Apollon Limassol FC is a Cypriot professional football club based in the city of Limassol. It was founded on 14 April 1954 by a group of young Cypriots with the aim of creating an athletic and cultural association. Since its establishment, Apollon has become one of the major clubs in Cypriot football, regularly competing in the top division and building a strong identity rooted in the city of Limassol. The club’s colours are blue and white, and it plays its home matches at the modern Alphamega Stadium.

Domestically, Apollon is considered one of the traditional “big teams” in Cyprus, having won multiple league titles, Cypriot Cups, and Super Cups. Its most successful periods came across different decades, especially in the 1990s and 2000s, when the club consistently challenged for honours. Apollon also has a strong rivalry with fellow Limassol clubs AEL and Aris, with derby matches being among the most intense fixtures in Cypriot football.

On the European stage, Apollon has been a regular participant in UEFA competitions, including the Champions League, Europa League, and Europa Conference League. While the club has not yet achieved a major European breakthrough, it has had several notable campaigns and group-stage appearances, helping raise its international profile. Apollon continues to be an important representative of Cypriot football in Europe and remains one of the most competitive clubs in the country.

name: Olympiakos Nicosia
content:
Olympiakos Nicosia FC is a Cypriot football club based in the capital city of Nicosia. It was founded on 1 June 1931 and is one of the founding members of the Cyprus Football Association. The club is known for its black and green colours and traditionally represents the Taktakalas area of Nicosia. Olympiakos plays its home matches at the GSP Stadium, one of the largest stadiums in Cyprus, which it shares with other major clubs in the city.

The club experienced its most successful period during the 1960s and early 1970s, often referred to as its “golden decade.” During this time, Olympiakos won three Cypriot First Division titles and also finished as runners-up multiple times. It also became one of the few Cypriot teams to participate in the Greek top division, reflecting its strong level during that era. Olympiakos has also won domestic cup competitions, adding to its historical achievements.

In European competitions, Olympiakos Nicosia has had limited but notable appearances, competing in UEFA tournaments such as the European Cup and UEFA competitions in later years. The club has faced strong opposition from major European teams but has also achieved occasional wins and draws that marked important milestones in its history. In recent decades, Olympiakos has moved between divisions but remains an important and traditional club in Cypriot football culture.

name: Enosis Neon Trust
content:
Enosis Neon Trust (also known as Trust AC) was a Cypriot football club based in Nicosia, founded in 1924. It was one of the founding members of the Cyprus Football Association and played a key role in the early development of organized football in the country. The club’s name came from the English word “trust,” and its colours were typically yellow and green. It played its home matches at the Old GSP Stadium in Nicosia.

Its legacy is remembered especially for its pioneering role and its early trophies, which helped shape the foundations of the modern Cypriot game.

name: Aris Limassol FC
content:
Aris Limassol FC is a Cypriot professional football club based in the city of Limassol. It was founded in 1930 and is one of the founding members of the Cyprus Football Association, making it one of the traditional clubs in Cypriot football history. The club’s colours are green and white, and it plays its home matches at the Alphamega Stadium. Throughout much of its history, Aris has been known as a modest club that frequently moved between the top division and the second tier.

For many decades, Aris struggled to establish itself among the strongest teams in Cyprus, often finishing in mid or lower table positions and facing multiple relegations. Despite this, the club had occasional highlights, including reaching the Cypriot Cup final in 1989, where it finished as runner-up. During this period, Aris was also known for having brief spells of stronger performance and attracting notable players, but consistency at the top level remained a challenge.

A major turning point in the club’s history came in the 2020s, when new investment and squad rebuilding significantly improved its competitiveness. Aris achieved its greatest success in the 2022–23 season by winning the Cypriot First Division for the first time in its history. This title marked a historic breakthrough for the club and secured its participation in European competitions, where it has since continued to grow its reputation on the international stage.

name: Çetinkaya Türk SK
content:
Çetinkaya Türk SK is a Turkish Cypriot football club based in North Nicosia. It was founded in 1930 and is one of the founding members of the original Cypriot First Division established in 1934. The club is historically known as “Kırmızı Şimşekler” (Red Thunders) and is widely regarded as one of the most decorated and important teams in Northern Cypriot football.

In its early history, Çetinkaya was the only Turkish Cypriot team competing in the Cypriot First Division alongside several Greek Cypriot clubs. It achieved major early success, including winning the Cypriot First Division, Cypriot Cup, and Cypriot FA Shield in the 1950s. The club also became a founding member of the Turkish Cypriot football system after 1955 and continued to dominate domestic competitions in Northern Cyprus over many decades.

Over time, Çetinkaya established itself as one of the most successful clubs in Northern Cyprus, collecting numerous league titles and cup trophies. It is historically significant for being the only club to have won major competitions in both the Cypriot football system and later Northern Cypriot competitions. Today, it remains an important traditional club in Nicosia with a strong historical legacy in Cypriot football culture.

name: Pafos FC
content:
Pafos FC was founded in 2014 after the merger of AEP Paphos and AEK Kouklia, with the goal of creating a unified and more competitive football club for the Paphos region. In its early years, the club began competing in the Cypriot Second Division and immediately set out to establish itself as a stable professional side. The project was built around local consolidation, combining resources and talent from the strongest teams in the area to form a single representative club for the district.

Between 2014 and 2017, Pafos FC experienced a turbulent sporting journey marked by promotion and relegation. The team achieved promotion to the Cypriot First Division in its debut season, but was relegated after just one year at the top level. However, the club quickly bounced back, returning to the First Division at the first attempt in 2016–17 after finishing near the top of the second tier. This period helped establish the club’s identity as a developing side capable of rapid recovery and progression within Cypriot football.

By the end of the early period, Pafos FC had begun to stabilise both competitively and structurally, setting the foundation for later investment and professionalisation. The club’s performances improved gradually, and it started to build a reputation as an ambitious modern project within Cypriot football. This early phase is widely seen as the formative stage that prepared the club for its later transformation into a consistent First Division contender.

name: Digenis Akritas Morphou FC
content:
Digenis Akritas Morphou FC is a Cypriot multi-sport club based in Morphou, founded on 23 April 1931. The club is named after the medieval Greek hero Digenis Akritas, who is also featured on its emblem. It is one of the oldest sports clubs in Cyprus and originally developed both cultural and athletic activities before forming its football section. Due to the lack of a suitable stadium in its early years, the football team did not immediately participate in official competitions.

The club joined the Cypriot football league system in 1968, starting in the Second Division, and quickly showed strong potential. It was promoted to the First Division after the 1969–70 season and reached one of its highest points in 1970–71, finishing as league runner-up and qualifying for European competition. Digenis became the first Cypriot club to compete in the UEFA Cup, where it faced AC Milan in the 1971–72 season.

Following the Turkish invasion of Cyprus in 1974, the club was displaced from Morphou and has since operated in exile, based in the southern part of the island. This event significantly affected its sporting performance, and the team spent many years moving between divisions. Despite this, Digenis has remained an active club and has achieved several lower-division successes, including promotions and cup wins, while also maintaining its basketball section and youth development programs.

name: Enosis Neon Paralimni FC
content:
Enosis Neon Paralimni FC is a Cypriot football club based in Paralimni, in the Famagusta District. It was founded in 1936 (with the official merger forming the club in 1944) after the union of two local teams, Heracles and People’s Love. The club is one of the traditional teams of Cypriot football and plays its home matches at the Tasos Markou Municipal Stadium. It is commonly known by its nickname “Vissini” (The Claret-Coloured Ones) due to its distinctive claret and blue colours.

During its early development, Enosis participated mainly in local competitions before gradually entering the Cypriot football league system in the 1960s. After joining official CFA competitions, the club quickly progressed through the Second Division and achieved promotion to the First Division in 1968–69. Over the following decades, Enosis established itself as a stable top-flight team, often competing to remain in the first division and occasionally challenging for higher positions in the league table.

In Cypriot football, Enosis Neon Paralimni has built a reputation as a resilient club with a strong local identity, even though it has not won major national trophies. It has spent many seasons in the First Division and is known for producing competitive squads that can challenge stronger teams on a good day. The club has also taken part in European competitions, though with limited success, reflecting its status as a historic but mid-level Cypriot side that remains an important part of the country’s football tradition.

name: Pezoporikos Larnaca FC
content:
Pezoporikos Larnaca FC was a Cypriot multi-sport club based in Larnaca, founded in 1927. It was one of the early football clubs on the island and later became a founding participant in Cypriot official football competitions. The club’s identity was closely linked with the city of Larnaca, and it also developed departments in other sports such as basketball and volleyball, making it an important athletic institution in Cypriot sport history.

In football, Pezoporikos experienced several successful periods, winning the Cypriot First Division twice and the Cypriot Cup once. It was also a regular contender in domestic competitions, finishing as runner-up on multiple occasions. One of its most notable achievements was participation in European competitions, although the club was unable to progress beyond the early rounds in UEFA tournaments.

In 1994, Pezoporikos Larnaca merged with another local club, EPA Larnaca, in order to form AEK Larnaca FC. This merger marked the end of the club as an independent entity but also ensured its legacy continued within the new unified team representing Larnaca. The history of Pezoporikos remains an important part of Cypriot football development, especially in the early and mid-20th century.

name: EPA Larnaca FC
content:
EPA Larnaca FC was a Cypriot football club based in the city of Larnaca. It was founded in 1930 through the merger of two local clubs, Pezoporikos and AMOL, and became one of the founding members of the Cyprus Football Association. The club played an important role in the early development of Cypriot football and participated in the first official Cypriot championship in 1934–35. EPA was also a multi-sport organization with departments in basketball and volleyball.

The club experienced its most successful period in the mid-1940s, when it achieved back-to-back domestic doubles, winning both the Cypriot First Division and the Cypriot Cup in 1944–45 and 1945–46. Over the following decades, EPA remained one of the stronger teams in Cyprus, winning multiple league titles and cup trophies and regularly competing at the top level of Cypriot football. It also represented Cyprus in Greek and European competitions during its strongest era.

In 1994, EPA Larnaca merged with another historic Larnaca club, Pezoporikos, to form AEK Larnaca FC. This merger was intended to unify football in the city and create a stronger modern club capable of competing at a higher level. Although EPA ceased to exist as an independent team, its legacy remains significant, as it contributed heavily to early Cypriot football success and is remembered as one of the traditional powerhouses of Larnaca football history.

name: Nea Salamis Famagusta FC
content:
Nea Salamis Famagusta FC is a Cypriot football club based in Larnaca, originally founded in 1948 in Famagusta. It was established by members who broke away from existing sports structures due to political and social divisions in Cypriot football at the time. The club is traditionally associated with the left-wing community and became one of the founding members of the Cyprus Amateur Football Federation before joining the official Cyprus Football Association in 1953. Its colours are red and white, and it is widely known for its strong identity and connection to the displaced Famagusta community.

name: Alki Larnaca FC
content:
Alki Larnaca FC was a Cypriot football club based in the city of Larnaca. It was founded in 1948 and became one of the well-known traditional teams in Cypriot football. The club played its home matches at the GSZ Stadium and was nicknamed “The Immortal” (Αθάνατη). Alki was considered an important part of Larnaca’s football identity and built a loyal local fan base over the decades.

Throughout its history, Alki spent many seasons in the Cypriot First Division and was known for being a competitive but inconsistent side. One of its best periods came in the late 1970s, when the club finished third in the league (1978–79 season) and also reached the Cypriot Cup final. Despite several strong cup runs, Alki never managed to win a major national trophy, finishing as runner-up in the Cypriot Cup five times.

In 2014, Alki Larnaca FC was dissolved due to severe financial problems and mounting debts, ending its long history in Cypriot football. The club had accumulated significant financial liabilities, which ultimately led to bankruptcy and closure. Although the team no longer exists in professional leagues, it remains a remembered part of Cypriot football history, especially in Larnaca, where it had a strong cultural and sporting presence.

name: APOP Kinyras FC
content:
APOP Kinyras FC was a Cypriot football club based in Peyia, in the Paphos District. It was formed in 2003 after the merger of two lower-league teams, APOP Peyias and Kinyras Empas. The club’s name combined the local APOP identity with “Kinyras,” a reference to the mythical King Kinyras, who is linked to the founding of ancient Paphos. It quickly became one of the fastest-rising clubs in Cypriot football in the 2000s.

Sporting success came rapidly for APOP Kinyras. The club climbed from the Third Division to the First Division in just a few seasons, winning consecutive promotions and establishing itself in the top flight. Its most famous achievement came in 2008–09, when it won the Cypriot Cup after defeating several major clubs, becoming the first team from the Paphos region to win a major national trophy.

name: Ethnikos Achna FC
content:
Ethnikos Achna FC is a Cypriot football club based in the village of Achna in the Famagusta District. It was founded in 1968 and is traditionally considered a small but stable club within Cypriot football. The team plays its home matches at the Dasaki Stadium in Dasaki Achnas and has developed a strong local identity despite representing a relatively small community.

Throughout its history, Ethnikos Achna has mostly alternated between the Cypriot First and Second Divisions, but it has spent a significant amount of time in the top flight since the early 1990s. The club’s best league finishes came in several seasons when it managed to reach fourth place, marking its peak domestic performances. It has also been a consistent mid-table side capable of challenging stronger Cypriot teams on good campaigns.

One of the club’s most notable achievements came in 2006, when it won the UEFA Intertoto Cup, becoming one of the competition’s final winners and earning qualification for the UEFA Cup. Ethnikos also reached the Cypriot Cup final twice (in 2002 and 2022), though it finished as runner-up on both occasions. Despite limited silverware, the club is respected for its European participation and occasional strong cup runs.

name: Ermis Aradippou FC
content:
Ermis Aradippou FC is a Cypriot football club based in Aradippou, near Larnaca. It was founded in 1958 and has traditionally been considered a small, community-based club within Cypriot football. The team plays its home matches at the local Aradippou Stadium and is known for its nickname “The Winged God.” Over the years, Ermis has mostly competed in the lower divisions but has had several spells in the Cypriot First Division.

Throughout its history, the club has moved between divisions, achieving promotion to the top tier multiple times, with its first appearances in the First Division coming in the 1980s. Ermis became more stable in the top flight during the late 2000s and early 2010s, managing to remain there for several consecutive seasons. However, like many smaller Cypriot clubs, it has struggled with consistency and has often faced relegation after short periods in the top division.

The club’s most notable achievement came in 2014, when it won the Cypriot Super Cup after defeating APOEL, marking the biggest trophy in its history. In the same period, Ermis also participated in European competition, entering the UEFA Europa League qualifiers, though it was eliminated in the early rounds. Despite its modest size, the club remains an important part of local football in Aradippou and is known for its resilience and occasional surprising results against stronger teams.
